items.stem: In the figure shown, the two lines are parallel. Angle 1 measures (x + 35) degrees, and angle 5 measures 65 degrees. What is the measure of angle 2?
items.explanation: Angles 1 and 5 are corresponding, so x + 35 = 65 and angle 1 measures 65 degrees. Angle 2 is supplementary to angle 1, so its measure is 180 - 65 = 115 degrees.

per_choice.correct: Angles 1 and 5 are corresponding, so x + 35 = 65 and angle 1 measures 65 degrees. Angle 2 is supplementary to angle 1, so its measure is 180 - 65 = 115 degrees.
per_choice.trap: 65 degrees results from identifying the corresponding angle but failing to use the adjacent supplementary angle; 30 degrees is x rather than the requested angle measure; 145 degrees results from subtracting 35 from 180 instead of using the full measure of angle 1.

items.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. The acute interior angle at the upper intersection on the right side of the transversal measures (3x + 11) degrees, and the interior angle at the lower intersection on the same side measures (5x + 9) degrees. A ray bisects the acute interior angle at the upper intersection. Which of the following must be true? I. The angle corresponding to the acute interior angle measures 71 degrees. II. The angle vertical to the lower-intersection interior angle measures 109 degrees. III. The angle between the bisecting ray and the transversal measures 54.5 degrees.
items.explanation: Same-side interior angles are supplementary, so (3x + 11) + (5x + 9) = 180, giving x = 20 and angles of 71 degrees and 109 degrees. Thus I and II are true; the bisector makes 35.5 degrees with the transversal, not 54.5 degrees, so III is false.

per_choice.correct: Same-side interior angles are supplementary, so (3x + 11) + (5x + 9) = 180, giving x = 20 and angles of 71 degrees and 109 degrees. Thus I and II are true; the bisector makes 35.5 degrees with the transversal, not 54.5 degrees, so III is false.
per_choice.trap: Choosing I and III only comes from confusing the half-angle with its complement; choosing I only or II only comes from applying the parallel-line relationship to one intersection but not recognizing that vertical angles preserve the 109-degree measure.

items.stem: Lines p and q are parallel. A transversal t intersects p at point P, and the acute angle formed by the ray of p pointing to the right and the ray of t pointing upward and to the right is bisected by a ray inside that angle. The acute angle between the bisecting ray and line q is 29 degrees. What is the measure of the original acute angle at P?
items.explanation: Because p and q are parallel, the bisecting ray makes the same acute angle, 29 degrees, with p as it does with q. The original angle is twice the bisected angle, so it measures 2(29) = 58 degrees.

per_choice.correct: Because p and q are parallel, the bisecting ray makes the same acute angle, 29 degrees, with p as it does with q. The original angle is twice the bisected angle, so it measures 2(29) = 58 degrees.

items.stem: At point P, lines AB and CD intersect, and angle APC measures 73 degrees. Which of the following must be true? I. Angle BPD measures 73 degrees. II. Angle APD measures 107 degrees. III. Angle BPC measures 73 degrees.
items.explanation: Angles APC and BPD are vertical angles, so I is true. Angles APC and APD are supplementary, so APD measures 107 degrees and II is true; angle BPC is also 107 degrees, so III is false.

per_choice.correct: Angles APC and BPD are vertical angles, so I is true. Angles APC and APD are supplementary, so APD measures 107 degrees and II is true; angle BPC is also 107 degrees, so III is false.

items.stem: In the figure shown, lines l and m are parallel and are cut by a transversal. Angle 1 measures (3x - 15) degrees and angle 5 measures 60 degrees. What is the value of x ?
items.explanation: Angles 1 and 5 sit in the same position at their own intersection, so they are corresponding angles and are equal when the lines are parallel. Solve 3x - 15 = 60 to get 3x = 75 and x = 25.
items.pattern: solve angle equation using corresponding angles

items.stem: Lines l and m are parallel. A transversal intersects l at B and m at E. Ray BD bisects angle ABC, and the angle formed by l and the transversal that corresponds to angle ABC is 80 degrees. If the measure of angle DBC is x + 10 degrees, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Because the corresponding angles formed by a transversal of parallel lines are congruent, angle ABC measures 80 degrees. Since ray BD bisects angle ABC, angle DBC measures 40 degrees. Therefore, x + 10 = 40, so x = 30.

per_choice.correct: Because the corresponding angles formed by a transversal of parallel lines are congruent, angle ABC measures 80 degrees. Since ray BD bisects angle ABC, angle DBC measures 40 degrees. Therefore, x + 10 = 40, so x = 30.
per_choice.trap: A student may treat angle DBC, which is only half of angle ABC, as the entire 80-degree angle and write x + 10 = 80, obtaining x = 70.

items.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One of the interior angles on the left side of the transversal measures 65 degrees. What is the measure of the other interior angle on that same side?
items.explanation: Same-side interior angles (co-interior angles) are supplementary when the lines are parallel, so the other angle is 180 - 65 = 115 degrees.

per_choice.correct: Same-side interior angles (co-interior angles) are supplementary when the lines are parallel, so the other angle is 180 - 65 = 115 degrees.

items.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two same-side interior angles measure (3x + 10) degrees and (5x - 30) degrees. What is the value of x ?
items.explanation: Same-side interior angles are supplementary: (3x + 10) + (5x - 30) = 180, so 8x - 20 = 180 and 8x = 200, giving x = 25.

items.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. The angle above the upper parallel line and to the right of the transversal measures (4x + 12) degrees. The same-side exterior angle below the lower parallel line and to the right of the transversal measures (5x + 33) degrees. What is the measure of the angle vertical to the first angle?
items.explanation: Same-side exterior angles are supplementary, so (4x + 12) + (5x + 33) = 180, giving x = 15. The first angle is therefore 72 degrees, and its vertical angle also measures 72 degrees.

per_choice.correct: Same-side exterior angles are supplementary, so (4x + 12) + (5x + 33) = 180, giving x = 15. The first angle is therefore 72 degrees, and its vertical angle also measures 72 degrees.

items.stem: Two lines intersect at a point, forming an angle of 37 degrees and its adjacent angle. A ray bisects the 37-degree angle, and a second ray bisects the adjacent angle. What is the measure of the smaller angle formed by the two bisecting rays?
items.explanation: The two adjacent angles form a linear pair, so their measures sum to 180 degrees. The angle between their bisectors is half of that sum, or 90 degrees, regardless of the original angle's measure.
items.pattern: angle between bisectors of adjacent angles

items.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An angle in the interior region on one side of the transversal measures (3x + 6) degrees, and its alternate interior angle measures (5x - 18) degrees. What is the measure of the angle adjacent to the first angle?
items.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal, so 3x + 6 = 5x - 18, which gives x = 12. The first angle is 42 degrees, so its adjacent angle is 180 - 42 = 138 degrees.

items.stem: At point P, rays PA and PB are opposite rays. On the same side of line AB, rays PC and PD occur in that order between PA and PB. The three adjacent angles measure (x + 10) degrees, (2x + 5) degrees, and (3x + 15) degrees, respectively. What is the measure of angle CPB?
items.explanation: Because PA and PB are opposite rays, the three adjacent angles sum to 180 degrees: (x + 10) + (2x + 5) + (3x + 15) = 180, so x = 25. Angle CPB consists of the second and third angles, giving 55 + 90 = 145 degrees.
items.pattern: partitioned straight angle with algebraic measures

items.stem: Lines p and q are parallel. A line t intersects both and makes an acute angle of 38 degrees with line p. A line s is perpendicular to t. What is the measure of the acute angle that line s makes with line q?
items.explanation: Since s is perpendicular to t, the acute angle between s and either parallel line is complementary to 38 degrees. Thus the angle is 90 - 38 = 52 degrees.

The same-side exterior angle below the lower parallel line and to the left of the transversal measures (4x + 25) degrees. What is the measure of the angle vertical to the first angle?
items.explanation: Same-side exterior angles are supplementary, so (3x + 15) + (4x + 25) = 180. This gives 7x + 40 = 180, so x = 20. The first angle measures 3(20) + 15 = 75 degrees, and its vertical angle also measures 75 degrees.

items.stem:
I. x = 22
II. The angle adjacent to the given angle at the intersection with p measures 77 degrees.
III. The angle below q and to the right of t measures 77 degrees.
items.stimulus: Lines p and q are parallel. A transversal t intersects p and q. The angle above p and to the left of t measures (3x + 11) degrees, and the angle below q and to the right of t measures (x + 55) degrees. Which of the following statements must be true?
items.explanation: The two given angles are alternate exterior angles, so they are congruent: 3x + 11 = x + 55, giving x = 22 and a given-angle measure of 77 degrees. Its adjacent angle is supplementary and measures 103 degrees, while the angle below q and to the right of t is 77 degrees, so I and III must be true.

per_choice.correct: The two given angles are alternate exterior angles, so they are congruent: 3x + 11 = x + 55, giving x = 22 and a given-angle measure of 77 degrees. Its adjacent angle is supplementary and measures 103 degrees, while the angle below q and to the right of t is 77 degrees, so I and III must be true.
per_choice.trap: A student may incorrectly make the adjacent angle equal to the given angle by applying the alternate-angle relationship to adjacent angles instead of to the two specified exterior angles.

items.stem: In the figure shown, lines p and q are parallel and are cut by a transversal. Angle 1 measures (3x + 11) degrees, and angle 5 measures 74 degrees. Which of the following statements is NOT true?
items.explanation: Angles 1 and 5 are corresponding, so 3x + 11 = 74 and x = 21. Thus angle 1 and its vertical angle, angle 3, measure 74 degrees; adjacent angles, including angle 2 and corresponding angle 6, measure 106 degrees.

per_choice.correct: Angles 1 and 5 are corresponding, so 3x + 11 = 74 and x = 21. Thus angle 1 and its vertical angle, angle 3, measure 74 degrees; adjacent angles, including angle 2 and corresponding angle 6, measure 106 degrees.
per_choice.trap: The incorrect choice results from treating angle 6 as corresponding to angle 5; angle 6 corresponds to angle 2, not angle 5.

items.stem: Two parallel lines p and q are cut by a transversal t. At the upper intersection, one obtuse angle measures (4x + 6) degrees, and the corresponding obtuse angle at the lower intersection measures (2x + 50) degrees. A ray bisects the first obtuse angle. Which of the following statements is NOT true?
choices: The acute angle between the bisecting ray and either parallel line measures 43 degrees.
Each of the corresponding obtuse angles measures 94 degrees.
Each angle adjacent to one of the obtuse angles measures 86 degrees.
items.explanation: Corresponding angles are congruent, so 4x + 6 = 2x + 50, giving x = 22 and an obtuse angle of 94 degrees. Its bisector forms an acute angle of 94/2 = 47 degrees with a parallel line, so the statement claiming 43 degrees is not true.

per_choice.correct: Corresponding angles are congruent, so 4x + 6 = 2x + 50, giving x = 22 and an obtuse angle of 94 degrees. Its bisector forms an acute angle of 94/2 = 47 degrees with a parallel line, so the statement claiming 43 degrees is not true.
per_choice.trap: The incorrect choice comes from bisecting the supplementary angle, 180 - 94 = 86, instead of bisecting the given 94-degree obtuse angle.
